blocks.text: Managing IT Assets in Excel for Mac

IT asset managers on Mac often deal with large datasets covering device serial numbers, purchase dates, and warranty status. Excel is effective for this because it is flexible and ubiquitous. You can quickly filter for assets nearing end-of-life or calculate depreciation schedules.
Essential Excel Tips for IT Asset Managers

items: Use Cmd + T to convert your range into a formal table. This makes sorting and filtering much easier when you add new hardware records.
Use Data Validation to create drop-down menus for status columns like Pending, Deployed, or Retired. This prevents typos in your inventory list.
Freeze your top row using View > Freeze Panes > Freeze Top Row. This keeps your headers visible as you scroll through hundreds of assets.
Use the XLOOKUP function to pull data from a master vendor list into your current inventory sheet. It is faster and more reliable than old VLOOKUP methods.

blocks.text: If you are struggling to find a specific feature in the ribbon, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where it is. Lazur will draw a circle around the button on your screen.
blocks.title: Find features quickly

blocks.text: A common mistake is letting Excel format serial numbers as scientific notation. If you have serials with many digits, select the column, right-click, and choose Format Cells > Text. This ensures your data remains accurate for audits.

Another issue is the lack of a consistent date format. Use the YYYY-MM-DD format for all purchase and warranty dates. This makes sorting chronologically simple and avoids confusion between different regional date standards.
Using Lazur with Excel on Mac

Lazur acts as an assistant that lives in your Mac notch. It helps you work faster by answering questions or guiding you through complex tasks. You do not need to hunt through menus for obscure functions anymore.
Pivot tables are your best friend for reporting. Select your data and go to Insert > PivotTable. You can summarize hardware counts by department or by location in seconds.

items: Group dates by month or year to track hardware refresh cycles.
Use Slicers to create interactive dashboards for your leadership team.
Conditional formatting can highlight assets that are more than three years old.

blocks.text: Excel has a limit of 1,048,576 rows. While this seems large, complex formulas can slow down your Mac if you have many tabs. Keep your workbooks lean by deleting unused rows and columns. If your file grows too large, consider breaking it into separate yearly files.
